lines: Four-operator phase-modulation oscillator with eleven fixed routings, polyphonic to 16 voices, each operator carrying a continuous waveshape morph, a wavefolder and self-feedback
Sets the pitch of the whole voice at a volt per octave, 0V giving 261.63Hz, and its channel count sets how many voices the module runs
Detunes every operator together, -100 to +100 cents
Scales the finished mix, silent at the left and unchanged at the right
Sets how much of each operator's output reaches the operator it modulates, none at the left and full at the right; it does not touch the carriers, which reach the mix at their own Level
Adds a tenth of its voltage to XMod after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Scales the Mod CV input before it is added to XMod, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Phase-modulates the finished mix: the module reads its own output back as a sine, shifts that phase by this voltage times the depth, and takes the sine again
Multiplied by the Ext PM input voltage to give the depth of external phase modulation, with the product held between 0 and 1; a negative product gives no modulation at all
Sets that operator's frequency: read as a ratio it steps from a quarter of the voice pitch to 31.5 times it, and read as a fixed frequency it sweeps from 1Hz to 9999Hz
Chooses whether that operator's Coarse knob is read as a ratio to the voice pitch or as a fixed frequency in Hz
Detunes that operator on its own, -100 to +100 cents
Sets that operator's output level, which is its share of the mix where the routing makes it a carrier and its modulation depth where the routing makes it a modulator
Adds a tenth of its voltage to that operator's Level after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's Level CV input before it is added, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Morphs that operator's waveform continuously from sine at the left through triangle and saw to pulse at the right, with the saw and pulse edges band-limited
Adds a tenth of its voltage to that operator's Warp after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's Warp CV input before it is added, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Wavefolds that operator's waveform, driving it from unchanged at the left to five times at the right into the folding curve chosen for that operator
Adds a tenth of its voltage to that operator's Fold after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's Fold CV input before it is added, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Feeds that operator's previous sample back into its own phase through a soft clip, none at the left and the full sample at the right
Adds a tenth of its voltage to that operator's FB after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's Feedback CV input before it is added, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
The sum of the operators the routing marks as carriers, each at its own Level, multiplied by 5 after the VCA; one carrier at full scale reaches about ±5V and several added together reach more
Note — the routing is picked on the algorithm display rather than by a knob: a left click steps to the next of the eleven and a right click opens a menu of them.
Note — the algorithm display is drawn rather than being a parameter, so clicking it never reaches a help line.
Note — each operator's folding curve is picked on the small box under its Fold knob: a left click steps through Sym, Asym and Soft.
Note — a right click on an operator's fold box opens a menu naming Symmetric, Asymmetric and Soft Clip. The box is drawn rather than a parameter, so clicking it reaches no help line.
Note — Op 1 comes up at full Level and the other three at zero, so a fresh module sounds only when the operators the routing feeds into Op 1 are turned up.
Note — every voice runs at two times oversampling and the carrier mix passes a DC blocker before the VCA.
Note — a mono cable, or one with fewer channels than V/OCT, is copied to every voice on all eighteen modulation inputs.
Note — this module is kept so that patches already using it keep loading, and it is hidden from the module browser. FourV2 is the current one.
Menu — Algorithm — on the algorithm display rather than the panel: lists the eleven fixed routings and sets the one in use
Menu — Fold Type: Symmetric, Asymmetric, Soft Clip — on the small box under each operator's Fold knob rather than the panel: sets the folding curve for that operator

FourMM.notes: Parameter 0, the algorithm, and parameters 50 to 53, the per-operator fold types, are declared and read by process() but are never given ParamWidgets: the algorithm is set through AlgoDisplay at src/Four/Four.cpp:361 and the fold types through FoldTypeDisplay at src/Four/Four.cpp:435, both plain Widgets. The panel SVG carries no lettering: every label is drawn in code by PanelLabels at src/Four/Four.cpp:552, which prints Four, Fine, VCA, V/Oct, XMod, Ext PM, Out, OP1 to OP4, and the row labels Freq, Level, Warp, Fold and FB. The Ext PM jack does two jobs at once — its voltage times the attenuator is clamped to 0..1 to give the depth (src/Four/engine.h:48), and the same voltage is the modulating signal (src/Four/engine.h:128) — which is why no negative field is written for it. Coarse in ratio mode snaps to 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and then every half step from 1 to 31.5 (src/Four/dsp.h:361); in fixed mode it is continuous, exponential from 1Hz to 9999Hz (src/Four/dsp.h:371).

lines: Four-operator phase-modulation oscillator with sixteen fixed routings drawn on a display, polyphonic to 16 voices, each operator carrying a continuous waveshape morph, a wavefolder and self-feedback
Sets the pitch of the whole voice at a volt per octave, 0V giving 261.63Hz, and its channel count sets how many voices the module runs
Picks one of the sixteen fixed routings, numbered 1 to 16, and the display beside it draws the one in use
Detunes every operator together, -100 to +100 cents
Scales the carrier mix, silent at the left and unchanged at the right; it is the only gain applied after the mix
Scales all phase modulation generated inside the module, both routed operator modulation and self-feedback, none at the left and full at the right; it does not touch carrier audio or the EXT PM jack
Raises or lowers PM DEPTH after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 0 and 1
Scales the PM DEPTH CV input before it is applied, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Phase-modulates every carrier directly, ahead of waveform generation, warping and folding; the shift is the input voltage times the attenuator times a tenth of a cycle
Scales the EXT PM input before it shifts carrier phase, none at the left and full at the right; it does not invert, so the polarity of the input is kept
Sets that operator's frequency: read as a ratio it snaps to one of fifteen, from four times the voice pitch down to an eighth of it, and read as a fixed frequency it sweeps from about 1Hz to 10kHz
Chooses whether that operator's COARSE knob is read as a ratio to the voice pitch or as a fixed frequency in Hz
Detunes that operator on its own, -100 to +100 cents, in both frequency modes
Chooses the folding curve that operator's FOLD knob drives into: symmetric, asymmetric or soft clip
Sets that operator's level at every destination: its share of the mix as a carrier, and its modulation depth as a modulator; the maker's tooltip and manual call this control Output
Raises or lowers that operator's LEVEL after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's LEVEL CV input before it is applied, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Morphs that operator's waveform continuously from sine at the left through triangle and saw to pulse at the right, with the saw and pulse edges band-limited
Raises or lowers that operator's WARP after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's WARP CV input before it is applied, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Wavefolds that operator's waveform, driving it from unchanged at the left to five times at the right into the curve its FOLD TYPE switch selects
Raises or lowers that operator's FOLD after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's FOLD CV input before it is applied, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Feeds that operator's previous sample back into its own phase through a soft clip, none at the left and the full sample at the right; PM DEPTH scales the result
Raises or lowers that operator's FEEDBACK after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 0 and 1
Scales that operator's FEEDBACK CV input before it is applied, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
The sum of the operators the routing marks as carriers, each at its own LEVEL, DC blocked and multiplied by 5 after MASTER; four carriers in phase can reach about ±20V
Note — patching a cable into any CV jack changes how its knob is read: the module assumes the source spans -10V to +10V, and remaps the knob plus the attenuverter's excursion into 0 to 1.
Note — that remapping keeps a CV waveform whole instead of flattening it against the ends of the range. With no cable, or with the attenuverter at centre, the knob is read unchanged.
Note — the lamp under MAIN OUT lights when the finished output on any voice reaches 10V either way, and holds for about 250ms. Nothing is clipped, limited or compressed: the lamp only reports.
Note — OP1 comes up at full LEVEL and the other three at zero, so a fresh module sounds only when the operators the routing feeds into OP1 are turned up.
Note — an operator whose LEVEL is zero keeps running, so turning its level back up continues its phase rather than restarting it.
Note — the fifteen ratios are, in knob order, 4:1, 3:1, 2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 2:3, 1:2, 1:3, 1:4, 1:5, 1:6, 1:7 and 1:8; 1:1 is the sixth and lands left of the knob's middle.
Note — each operator has its own small display showing the ratio or the fixed frequency its COARSE knob has reached.
Note — every voice runs at two times oversampling, and the routing display and the frequency displays report rather than control.
Note — a mono cable, or one with fewer channels than V/OCT, is copied to every voice on all eighteen modulation inputs.

FourV2.notes: The panel prints LEVEL on the four operator level knobs, while configParam at src/FourV2/FourV2.cpp:241 names them Op N Output and the README calls the control OUTPUT; the panel is followed in the line and the disagreement named there. The panel SVG carries the operator artwork but the lettering is drawn in code by FourV2PanelLabels at src/FourV2/FourV2.cpp:516, which prints Four V2, ALGO, TUNE, PM DEPTH, MASTER, EXT PM, V/OCT, MAIN OUT, OP1 to OP4, COARSE, MODE, FINE, FOLD TYPE, LEVEL, WARP, FOLD and FEEDBACK. The OVER lamp is configLight-named OVER at src/FourV2/FourV2.cpp:304 but no OVER lettering is drawn; it is an unlabelled red lamp under MAIN OUT, and lights cannot be clicked for help, so it is covered by a Note. All 54 parameters have widgets, unlike Four. Ratio mode snaps the continuous 0..14 COARSE value to one of the fifteen ratios in src/FourV2/model.h:33; fixed mode maps the same 0..14 exponentially to expf(coarse/14 * ln 10000), which is 1Hz at the left and 10000Hz at the right (src/FourV2/model.h:89). No module has a panel context menu anywhere in this plugin.

lines: Multi-mode filter running one of twelve responses at a time, polyphonic to 16 voices, with a saturating drive stage ahead of the filter
Sets the filter corner, 20Hz at the left and 20kHz at the right
Multiplies the corner by two raised to its own voltage, after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 20Hz and 20kHz
Scales the Cutoff CV input before it shifts the corner, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Sets the resonance at the corner, sweeping the filter damping from 0.707 at the left to 0.01 at the right
Raises the resonance after the attenuverter beside it, each volt at a full attenuverter taking 0.2 off the damping, and the damping is held between 0.01 and 0.707
Scales the Reso CV input before it changes the damping, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Sets the gain into a soft-clipping stage ahead of the filter, unity at the left and ten times at the right
Adds a tenth of its voltage to the drive after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Scales the Drive CV input before it is added to the drive, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
The signal to be filtered; its channel count sets how many voices the module runs, and it is divided by 5 on the way in and multiplied by 5 again at the output
The filtered signal, carrying one channel per voice of the input
Note — the response is picked on the mode display rather than by a knob: a left click steps to the next of the twelve and a right click opens a menu of them.
Note — the mode display is drawn rather than being a parameter, so clicking it never reaches a help line.
Note — the twelve responses are LP 6dB, LP 12dB, LP 24dB, HP 6dB, HP 12dB, HP 24dB, BP, BP+, Notch, Notch+, AP and AP+.
Note — the four responses marked with a plus run two identical two-pole sections in series, doubling the slope of the plain one, and Reso has no effect on the two 6dB responses, which are one-pole.
Note — changing the response clears the filter state on every voice, so a note sounding at the time restarts rather than crossfades.
Note — a mono cable, or one with fewer channels than the input, is copied to every voice on each of the three CV jacks.
Note — this module is kept so that patches already using it keep loading, and it is hidden from the module browser. VortexV2 is the current one.
Menu — Filter Mode — on the mode display rather than the panel: lists the twelve responses and sets the one in use

lines: Multi-mode filter with twelve outputs running at once, one response each, polyphonic to 16 voices, with a saturating drive stage ahead of them
Sets the filter corner, 20Hz at the left and 20kHz at the right, with every octave given the same amount of travel
Scales the Cutoff CV input before it shifts the corner, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Sets the resonance at the corner, sweeping the filter damping from 0.707 at the left to 0.01 at the right
Scales the Reso CV input before it changes the damping, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Sets the gain into a soft-clipping stage ahead of the filters, unity at the left and ten times at the right
Scales the Drive CV input before it is added to the drive, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Scales the V/OCT input before it shifts the corner, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at full positive, so the corner tracks a volt per octave straight away
The signal to be filtered; its channel count sets how many voices the module runs, and it is divided by 5 on the way in and multiplied by 5 again at each output
Multiplies the corner by two raised to its own voltage, after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 20Hz and 20kHz
Raises the resonance after the attenuverter beside it, each volt at a full attenuverter taking 0.2 off the damping, and the damping is held between 0.01 and 0.707
Adds a tenth of its voltage to the drive after the attenuverter beside it, and the total is held between 0 and 1
Shifts the corner a volt per octave after the attenuverter beside it, and the result is held between 20Hz and 20kHz
A one-pole low pass of the driven signal, 6dB per octave; RESO has no effect on it
A two-pole low pass of the driven signal, 12dB per octave, damped by RESO
Two two-pole low pass sections in series, 24dB per octave, each damped by RESO
A one-pole high pass of the driven signal, 6dB per octave; RESO has no effect on it
A two-pole high pass of the driven signal, 12dB per octave, damped by RESO
Two two-pole high pass sections in series, 24dB per octave, each damped by RESO
A two-pole band pass of the driven signal centred on the corner, damped by RESO
Two identical band pass sections in series, narrowing the band that the single one passes
A two-pole notch of the driven signal, cutting the corner and passing either side of it, damped by RESO
Two identical notch sections in series, deepening the cut that the single one makes
A two-pole all pass of the driven signal, passing every frequency and shifting phase around the corner, damped by RESO
Two identical all pass sections in series, doubling the phase shift the single one applies
Note — an output with nothing patched into it is reset and skipped, so its filter starts from silence when a cable is plugged back in and it costs nothing while unpatched.
Note — a mono cable, or one with fewer channels than the audio input, is copied to every voice on each of the four CV jacks.
Note — the drive stage is a soft clip bounded at plus or minus 3, so a hot input or a feedback build cannot run away.

VortexV2.notes: The cutoff CV jack is scaled exactly as the V/OCT jack is, by two raised to the volts, so both are marked as pitch. The difference is the attenuverter default: V/OCT comes up at full positive and the cutoff CV attenuverter at zero. The corner is clamped to 20Hz..20000Hz after both are applied.

lines: Dual voltage-window comparator: each channel reports whether its signal is inside a window you set, gives its position within that window as a voltage, and fires a trigger at each boundary crossing
Sets the midpoint of that channel's window, -5V at the left and +5V at the right
Sets the total span of that channel's window, 0V at the left and 10V at the right, with the boundaries half of that span either side of the midpoint; it starts at 5V
Scales that channel's CTR CV input before it is added to the CENTER knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Scales that channel's WID CV input before it is added to the WIDTH knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
The voltage Channel A compares with its window; its channel count sets how many voices Channel A runs
Moves the midpoint of Channel A's window, added to the CENTER knob through the attenuverter beside it
Changes the total span of Channel A's window, added to the WIDTH knob through the attenuverter beside it, and the resulting span is held between 1mV and 20V
The voltage Channel B compares with its window; with nothing patched here Channel B reads Channel A's SIGNAL input, in full for a polyphonic cable
Moves the midpoint of Channel B's window through the attenuverter beside it; with nothing patched here Channel B reads Channel A's CTR CV input
Changes the total span of Channel B's window through the attenuverter beside it; with nothing patched here Channel B reads Channel A's WID CV input
10V while that channel's signal is inside its window and 0V otherwise, with a signal resting exactly on a boundary counted as inside
10V while that channel's signal is outside its window and 0V while it is inside
Where that channel's signal falls within its window: -5V at the low boundary, 0V at the midpoint and +5V at the high boundary, clamped to those limits beyond them
A 1ms 10V trigger when that channel's signal crosses the low boundary upward, entering the window from below
A 1ms 10V trigger when that channel's signal crosses the high boundary upward, leaving the window above
A 1ms 10V trigger when that channel's signal crosses the low boundary downward, leaving the window below
A 1ms 10V trigger when that channel's signal crosses the high boundary downward, entering the window from above
10V while both channels are inside their windows, 0V otherwise
10V while either channel is inside its window, 0V while neither is
10V while exactly one of the two channels is inside its window, 0V otherwise
A held 0V or 10V that flips on every rising edge of XOR, so it changes each time the two channels go from agreeing to disagreeing; it starts low and is not saved with the patch
Note — crossings are measured against the window as it stands at that moment, so modulating CENTER or WIDTH across a stationary signal fires the same triggers as moving the signal would.
Note — a jump that clears the whole window in one step fires both boundary triggers, in the order they were passed.
Note — the starting state is taken silently: no trigger is produced when the module is added to a patch or reset.
Note — a hysteresis of 1mV is applied to every boundary test, so a noisy signal lying on a boundary does not chatter between states.
Note — the slim rail between each channel's SIGNAL and POSITION sockets draws the first voice on a fixed -10V to +10V scale, with ticks marking +10V, 0V and -10V.
Note — on that rail a translucent band marks the window, lines mark its low boundary, midpoint and high boundary, and a short pale line marks the signal. Voltages past either end stop there.
Note — each channel runs up to 16 voices, counted from its own SIGNAL input, and a mono CTR CV or WID CV cable is copied to every voice.
Note — the four shared logic outputs run at the larger of the two channels' voice counts, with the shorter channel's first voice copied across.
Note — this module is kept so that patches already using it keep loading, and it is hidden from the module browser. BrinkV2 is the current one.

Brink.notes: The window is built in src/Brink/dsp.h:137 as centre minus half the span to centre plus half the span, so WIDTH is the total span and not a distance from the midpoint. HYSTERESIS at src/Brink/dsp.h:12 is 0.001, applied to every boundary test in advance_region. The four boundary triggers last 0.001 seconds, set in start_pulse at src/Brink/dsp.h:215. The channel-A-to-B normalling is done by substituting the Input object itself rather than a voltage, so a polyphonic cable on Channel A carries across in full, and each of the three normals is broken independently by patching the matching Channel B jack. The panel SVG carries no lettering: every label is drawn in code by PanelLabels at src/Brink/Brink.cpp:540, which prints CHANNEL A, CHANNEL B, CENTER, WIDTH, SIGNAL, POSITION, CTR CV, WID CV, INSIDE, OUTSIDE, LOW, HIGH, AND, OR, XOR and TOGGLE, with an up arrow beside one trigger row and a down arrow beside the other.
